messages.author: d359b7da0a3070cd
messages.subject: Allele specific copy number estimates
parts:
Hi Henrik,

I have been using aroma.affymetrix to implement a method of my own for
estimating allele specific copy numbers from Affy 50K and 250K arrays,
and have found it very useful, but now I want to compare results
empirically with the method of the Bengtsson et al. (2008) paper.
There are vignettes for total copy number analysis, but not for allele
specific copy number analysis, and as there are so many possible
correction and normalisation procedures, I am not sure which ones to
use and in what order.

In a post of about 2 weeks ago you said that you planned to "put up a
CRMA (v1) vignette illustrating the exact steps in the Bengtsson et
al. (2008) paper or CRMA preprocessing (our preferred method) of 500K
(and before), but short of time... " Any news on this? Is there
somewhere I can look in the mean time for ideas?

Mike

> I have been using aroma.affymetrix to implement a method of my own for
> estimating allele specific copy numbers from Affy 50K and 250K arrays,
> and have found it very useful, but now I want to compare results
> empirically with the method of the Bengtsson et al. (2008) paper.
> There are vignettes for total copy number analysis, but not for allele
> specific copy number analysis, and as there are so many possible
> correction and normalisation procedures, I am not sure which ones to
> use and in what order.
>
> In a post of about 2 weeks ago you said that you planned to "put up a
> CRMA (v1) vignette illustrating the exact steps in the Bengtsson et
> al. (2008) paper or CRMA preprocessing (our preferred method) of 500K
> (and before), but short of time... " Any news on this? Is there
> somewhere I can look in the mean time for ideas?

If you do 'combineAlleles=FALSE' in the setup of the RmaCnPlm, you
will get allele-specific estimates. You can then continue with
fragment-length normalization and segmentation as is.

Also, in this case extractTheta(cesN) will return (thetaA, thetaB)
estimates. When you do combineAlleles=TRUE, you will get the total
theta estimates.

You should expect to get even better results when the CRMA v2
preprocessing method comes out, because it will control also for
allelic imbalances in addition to other things.

Hope this helps you get going.

Henrik
